A_target.statement:
Let $V$ be a [[Definition:Vector Space|vector space]] of finite [[Definition:Dimension of Vector Space|dimension]] $n$ over a [[Definition:Field (Abstract Algebra)|field]] $K$, with [[Definition:Basis (Linear Algebra)|basis]] $\tuple {e_1, \ldots, e_n}$.
Then the [[Definition:Linear Functional|linear functionals]] $e_i^*$ defined by:
:$\map {e_i^*} {e_j} = \delta_{i j}$
form a [[Definition:Basis (Linear Algebra)|basis]] of the [[Definition:Algebraic Dual|dual space]] $V^*$, and $\dim V^* = n$.

B_source.statement:
Let $\tuple {e_1, \ldots, e_n}$ be a [[Definition:Basis (Linear Algebra)|basis]] of $V$.
Then every $v \in V$ can be written uniquely as:
:$\displaystyle v = \sum_{i \mathop = 1}^n \lambda_i e_i$

substitutions.the coordinates of a vector: the values of the dual basis functionals on it

derived.spanning and independence of the basis: spanning and independence of the dual basis

validity_conditions: Uniqueness of coordinates is what makes each coordinate-extraction map well defined, and linearity of the coordinates makes it a functional.
The dual functionals are independent because applying a vanishing combination to a basis vector isolates one coefficient.
They span the dual only in finite dimension: for an infinite-dimensional space the analogous functionals do not span the full dual, so the dimension statement fails.
proof_plan: For each $i$, define $e_i^*: V \to K$ by $\map {e_i^*} v = \lambda_i$, the $i$th coordinate of $v$.

By uniqueness of coordinates, $e_i^*$ is [[Definition:Well-Defined Mapping|well-defined]].
Coordinates of $\alpha v + \beta w$ are $\alpha \lambda_i + \beta \mu_i$, so $e_i^*$ is [[Definition:Linear Transformation|linear]].

Suppose $\displaystyle \sum_i c_i e_i^* = 0$.
Evaluating at $e_j$ gives $c_j = 0$.
Hence the $e_i^*$ are [[Definition:Linearly Independent Set|linearly independent]].

For $f \in V^*$:
:$\displaystyle f = \sum_{i \mathop = 1}^n \map f {e_i} e_i^*$
as both sides agree on each $e_j$.
Hence the $e_i^*$ span $V^*$, and $\dim V^* = n$.
{{qed}}
